name: Pet shops and pet supplies
shape_facts: What they sell: food and supplies only, or also live animals (birds, fish, small pets) and services (grooming, boarding).
Imported vs local food brands, and buying direct vs distributor.
Channels: walk-in, WhatsApp/Instagram delivery, website, Talabat/Noon/Instashop/Amazon, subscriptions.
Delivery fleet: own riders or courier.
Whether a vet works with or near the shop (referral only).
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems such as food stock and expiry, repeat delivery orders, grooming bookings, live-animal care workload, supplier imports and staff. pi gives no veterinary, nutritional, medication, dosing or breeding advice, and no advice on animal import or export permits or wildlife law. If an animal is in distress, pi suggests contacting a vet urgently; if people are in danger (bites, fire), pi points to emergency services. pi does not record customers’ or pets’ owners’ personal details, and refuses to help with trade in protected or wild species.

vocabulary.boarding: looking after pets while owners are away
vocabulary.aquarium / tank: fish tanks, with filters, pumps and accessories
vocabulary.livestock (aquatic): trade term for live fish and invertebrates
vocabulary.prescription diet: vet-prescribed food (shop only stocks; vet decides)

mix: Do you mainly sell food and supplies, or also animals and services like grooming?
Which part brings in most of the money?
stock: Which items run out most often?
How do you find out before a customer asks?
expiry and storage: How do you check expiry dates on food?
Where is stock kept and does anything get damaged there?
repeat orders: Do customers buy the same food every month?
delivery: Who delivers, your riders or a courier?
What goes wrong most with deliveries?
live animals: Who looks after the animals in the shop each day?
How do you check it’s been done?
suppliers: Is most of your stock imported or local?
What happens when a shipment is delayed?
marketplaces: Do you sell on any delivery apps or marketplaces?
owner view: At month end, how do you see what each category earned?

seasons: In the UAE: summer heat affects deliveries and live-animal handling, while summer travel drives boarding and pet relocation (relocation itself is out of pi’s scope). Cooler months bring outdoor activity and accessories, along with Black Friday/White Friday, and Ramadan and Eid travel for boarding. In PK: Eid holidays drive boarding demand, and imported-food availability swings with currency moves and import restrictions; summer heat matters for fish and birds. Spring is the main bird and aquarium season. In Canada: holiday season gifting, summer boarding and Black Friday. Subscriptions smooth demand across the year.
care: No veterinary, medical, dosing, diet or breeding advice; animal in distress → contact a vet urgently.
Danger to people (serious bite, fire, chemical exposure from aquarium products) → emergency services.
Refuse any help with trade in protected, wild or illegally imported animals, or bypassing import/quarantine controls.
Do not advise on permits for animal import/export, licensing or welfare law; record effort only.
Animal welfare concerns raised by the owner: record the operational issue (checklists, staffing) without judgement; refuse to help conceal mistreatment.
Do not record customers’ names, addresses or pet records.
Staff suspicions recorded by role only.
build_ideas: Food stock by brand, size and expiry with first-expiry-first-out alerts and reorder suggestions.
Repeat-order reminders on WhatsApp timed to each customer’s usual cycle (with consent), with one-tap reorder.
Subscription/autoship list with delivery schedule and payment status.
Delivery planner grouping orders by area, with rider assignment and proof of delivery.
Grooming and boarding booking calendar with groomer schedules and reminders.
Grooming job card with intake condition notes and photos.
Live-animal daily care checklist (feeding, water changes, temperature) with staff sign-off.
Live-stock loss log for fish/birds with cost per month.
Marketplace stock sync for delivery apps.
Supplier tracker for imported shipments with expected dates.
Margin by brand after delivery costs.
Owner daily read: sales, stockouts, orders due, bookings.

exchange.text: Our regular customers buy the same food every month, but if we’re out of stock they just go to another shop.
That’s a hard way to lose a regular. Noted: customers switch shops when their usual food is out of stock. Is it mostly imported brands that run out?
Noted. When you place an order with the distributor, how do you decide how much to buy?
Honestly, I just look at the shelf.
Got it, noted that ordering is done by looking at the shelf. How long does a delivery from the distributor usually take to arrive?
